<description>
If a flush that prunes block files fails before the block index write, the files are already marked pruned in memory, but `setFilesToPrune` is a local in `FlushStateToDisk()`. The next successful flush writes the pruned file info and never deletes the blk/rev files. Only `ScanAndUnlinkAlreadyPrunedFiles()` deletes them, at the next startup.

This is number 7 of ryanofsky's [post-merge review of #35714](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714#pullrequestreview-5697890316). The block file flush failure from #35714 and the blocks directory `CheckDiskSpace()` failure both return before that write.

I worked on this because it lets me test my kernel pruning refactor (#36738, for #35627 and kernel-node/kernel-node#111) against the issue he describes. The refactor moves the flush, block index write and file deletion that a pruning flush runs from `FlushStateToDisk()` into `WriteBlockStorage()`, and no unit test ran that sequence in prune mode. I rebased the refactor onto this branch, and the new tests pass on each of its commits.

The first three commits add tests that pass on master. The unit test fixtures apply `-prune` and `-fastprune` from `extra_args`, `chainstate_flush_failure_boundary` checks that a flush after a failed one writes what was skipped, and `prune_flush_failure` shows that a failed prune flush still leaves its files on disk after a retry.

The last commit keeps the selected files in `BlockManager` and deletes them after the next block index write. If that write fails they are dropped with the dirty entries, which means a file is only deleted once it is marked pruned on disk. Pending files don't force a write. The next flush that writes deletes them.

The disk-space failure and automatic pruning take the same path but have no test. Neither does the `FindNextBlockPos()` line that drops a file from the pending set when a block is written to it, which can happen after an assumeutxo snapshot validates.
</description>

<new_statements>
[2026-11-19] rc:4634832807 inline on src/validation.cpp by pzafonte (contributor) (edited 2026-11-19):
Sorry for the delay in response. You're right that the retry doesn't delete them. File 0 already has `nSize == 0`, so `FindFilesToPruneManual()` selects nothing and a `NONE` flush doesn't write. The files are still in `m_files_to_unlink` and the next flush that writes deletes them.

That's deliberate on my part and I believe it matches item 6 of ryanofsky's [post-merge review](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714#pullrequestreview-5697890316) where skipped writes are kept in memory until a later flush writes them. A `NONE` retry doesn't write the dirty block index or coins either. In the node a failed flush requests shutdown, and the shutdown flush calls `ForceFlushStateToDisk()`, which uses `FORCE_FLUSH`, which is the retry that actually runs, so it's what the test uses. Item 9 suggests documenting that kernel users should stop the same way.

Edit: item 4 of the same review fits better (arejula27 is [working on it](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35731#issuecomment-7017968242) in #35731). A `false` from `FlushStateToDisk()` only means the disk write failed, and in-memory state is still valid. `pruneblockchain` already works that way. It logs the failure and returns the prune height from memory. The files are pruned in memory, and the disk catches up on the next write.
[2026-11-19] rc:4634911169 inline on src/node/blockstorage.cpp by pzafonte (contributor) (edited 2026-11-19):
Yes, after an assumeutxo snapshot validates. There's no single `m_last_blockfile` anymore. `m_blockfile_cursors` has a `NORMAL` and an `ASSUMED` cursor, and until restart the `NORMAL` one still points at the last file the background chainstate wrote to. Once the snapshot is validated, `GetPruneRange()` starts at 0 and that file isn't `MaxBlockfileNum()` so it can be pruned. A block below the snapshot height (e.g. from `getblockfrompeer`) then goes into it at offset 0, because `PruneOneBlockFile()` reset its `CBlockFileInfo`. If the flush that pruned the file failed, it would still be pending, and without this line the next write would delete it with that block in it. I can put this in the comment above the line.

With regard to `rb+` master reuses the file the same way after a failed prune flush, since it never deletes the file. The old data after the new block isn't read, because reads use the stored positions. Overwriting the head is a problem if the node crashes before the next write, because the index on disk still lists the old blocks there. But I think that can be a fix in a separate / followup PR.
</new_statements>
